The option Custom in IdsMTimestampOption shall enable the timestamp feature and determines that the source of the timestamp is provided by the application software.

Timestamps are optional If the parameter IdsMTimestampSupport equals FALSE, the timestamp feature is disabled and IdsM shall not add a timestamp to a QSEv . The IdsM shall ignore timestamps provided via the timestamp parameter of the event reporting interface.

Timestamps provided by the stack If IdsMTimestampOption is set to "‘AUTOSAR"’ and the SEv is reported without a timestamp parameter, then IdsM shall add a timestamp from the StbM to the stored and transmitted QSEvs.

Timestamp provided via event reporting interface If the timestamp feature is enabled and the SEv is reported with a timestamp parameter via the services IdsM_ReportSecurityEvent , then IdsM shall use this provided timestamp parameter for transmission or storage of the QSEv .

Timestamp provided via application software If IdsMTimestampOption is set to "‘Custom"’, and the SEv is reported without a timestamp parameter, then IdsM shall request a timestamp from the application via the TimestampProvider callback and add the received timestamp to the QSEv .

Truncation of timestamp parameter If the SEv is reported with a timestamp parameter, then IdsM shall truncate this value by the 2 most-significant bits, i.e., only keep the 62 least-significant bits for further use.

If the option Custom in IdsMTimestampOption is enabled, the IdsM shall use the Client Server Interface IdsM_RequestCustomTimestamp with the operation Get , which the application shall implement, to request a timestamp from the SW-C via the Require Port CustomTimestamp .

Timestamp not provided via event reporting interface. If the timestamp feature is enabled and the SEv is reported without a timestamp parameter, then IdsM shall set the option bit for the timestamp in protocol header to 0 before the transmission or storage of the QSEv .
Timestamp Support If the parameter IdsMTimestampSupport equals TRUE, the timestamp feature is enabled. Note: It is not mandatory to configure IdsMTimestampOption when IdsMTimestampSupport is TRUE.

The configuration of a SEv IdsMEvent shall contain a list of data sinks which are used for the resulting QSEv .
Forwarding Security Events The IdsM shall provide the functionality for forwarding qualified on-board security events QSEvs to other ECUs via the PduR module.

QSEv transmission The IdsM shall be able to use the sink IdsR for the configured events. The IdsMSinkIdsR indicates that the corresponding QSEv shall be sent via PduR in a IDS Message to the communication network.

Authenticating QSEv The IdsM shall be able to attach a cryptographic authenticator , with the same data format, to each QSEv . The authentication feature is optional and shall be activated or deactivated globally for all QSEvs by setting the parameter IdsMAuthenticatorSupport to TRUE or FALSE.

AuthenticatorLength The IdsM’s parameter IdsMAuthenticatorLength shall define the length in bytes of the authenticator calculated by the crypto services. It shall be configured when the authentication feature is activated.

GenerateAuthenticator In order to generate an authenticator by a Csm job IdsMCsmJobReference , the authentication generation shall be triggered by calling the Csm function Csm_ SignatureGenerate or Csm_MacGenerate depending on the selected IdsMAuthenticatorType .

SynchronousAuthenticatorGeneration If the authenticator is generated by a synchronous Csm job IdsMCsmJobReference , when the function Csm_SignatureGenerate or Csm_MacGenerate returns, the authenticator shall be immediately available.

AsynchronousAuthenticatorGeneration If the authenticator is generated by an asynchronous Csm job IdsMCsmJobReference , the IdsM shall be informed about the generation of the authenticator by Csm via the Csm notification callback function IdsM_CsmNotification .
Enable/Disable QSEv Transmission IdsM shall support enabling and disabling the forwarding of qualified security events to the sink IdsR during run-time over the API IdsM_TransmissionSetState .

Transmission State The IdsM shall be informed by the BswM module about the transmission state with the callback service IdsM_TransmissionSetState . This information shall be used when a QSEv is generated for transmission.
Transmission ON IdsM shall forward QSEvs to the sink IdsR only when the transmission is enabled IDSM_TRANSMISSION_STATE_ON .

Deprecated Reporting API Status: DRAFT IdsM shall use the IDS protocol version 1 to generate the QSEv for security events that were reported with context data over the deprecated services IdsM_SetSecurityEventWithContextData, IdsM_SetSecurityEventWithTimestampCountContextData and IdsM_SetSecurityEventWithCountContextData.
New Reporting API IdsM shall use the newest IDS protocol version to generate the QSEv for security events that were reported with the service IdsM_ReportSecurityEvent .
Context Data Size Limit A SEvs reported by a SW-C shall define a maximum number of bytes for the transmission of the context data. IdsMEventMaxContextDataSize .

No additional Interface Option Status: OBSOLETE The SW-C Service Port Interface shall not provide additional information other than the optional context data when the option None is configured in IdsMAdditionalParameterOption.
Additional Interface Option: Count Status: OBSOLETE The SW-C Service Port Interface shall be extended by the parameter count when the option Count is configured in IdsMAdditionalParameterOption.

Additional Interface Option: Count and timestamp Status: OBSOLETE The SW-C Service Port Interface shall be extended by the parameters count and timestamp when the option CountTimestamp is configured in IdsMAdditionalParameterOption.

NULL-Pointer valid for parameter for Timestamp-Pointer For an IdsMExternalEventId , when IdsMEventEnableTimestampReporting is False and the IdsMExternalEventId is in range 0x8000 - 0xFFFE, IdsM shall offer a service interface for reporting the security event with a possibility to provide NULL_PTR to the timestampPtr argument as specified in [SWS_IdsM_91044]…

IF-PDU The IdsM shall send its data via an interface PDU ( IF - PDU ) if the complete IDS Message with its additional IDS Message Authenticator , if available, fits in a single Bus-PDU . Configured in: IdsMIfTxPdu .
Transport Protocol Otherwise, if the data does not fit in a single IF - PDU frame, it shall be send via transport protocol using TP - PDUs. Configured in: IdsMTpTxPdu .

Pdu Transmission After the IdsM has processed the SEvs, the resulting QSEvs which have passed the filtering and have the IdsMSinkIdsR configured, shall be transmitted using the service PduR_IdsMTransmit .
Consider Tx Confirmation before next Transmit IdsM shall not call PduR_IdsMTransmit again before IdsM_TpTxConfirmation or IdsM_TxConfirmation have been called.
Using Tx Confirmation The IdsM shall receive the confirmation for the complete transmission of the IF upper layer Tx-Pdu by the PduR Module with the service IdsM_TxConfirmation .

Segmented Transmission The IdsM shall be able to transmit segmented PDUs with the service IdsM_CopyTxData . The function shall be called several times, each call to this function shall transmit a segment of the Tx-PDU , until it has been completely sent.
Using Tx Confirmation for Segmented Transmission The IdsM shall receive the confirmation of the transmission of a segmented PDU by the PduR Module with the service IdsM_TpTxConfirmation .

Retry Handling If the transmission request over PduR_IdsMTransmit is declined, i.e., the API does not return E_OK , IdsM shall wait a time period of IdsMTransmissionRetryDelay and attempt to transmit the same message again.
The IdsM shall provide a functionality for persisting on-board QSEvs, with their corresponding optional fields: context data and timestamp in Dem / Sem .
The IdsM shall be able to use the sink Dem / Sem for the configured events. The Sem sink indicates that the corresponding QSEv shall be stored in the Dem ’s user defined memory: Sem .
{DRAFT} The data stored in Dem / Sem is the complete IDS Message with its mandatory and optional fields.

Dem Event referenced by IdsM Event IdsMEvent shall have a mapping to DemEventParameter via configuration parameter IdsMDemEventReference . Every IdsMEvent that is intended to be sinked to the Dem / Sem shall have a valid IdsMDemEventReference not necessarily unique.

Dem API If IdsMSinkDem for an IdsMEvent is set to true, then IdsM shall report to Dem by calling API Dem_SetEventStatus with arguments EventId as the DemEventId of the referenced DemEventParameter over IdsMDemEventReference and EventStatus as DEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED .
Dem Callback With Freeze Frame IdsM shall provide complete IDS Message with its mandatory and optional fields as freeze frame data of the reported Dem event via a callback function IdsM_DemReadQSEv .

API Call Sequence IdsM shall call Dem_SetEventStatus at most once before IdsM_DemReadQSEv has been called by Dem to fetch the freeze frame data. This is necessary for Dem to fetch the correct QSEv as the freeze frame record.
Finish Call Sequence Once Dem has fetched the freeze frame data, IdsM shall call Dem_SetEventStatus with EventStatus as DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PASSED .
The IdsM shall be able to persist the parameter " Reporting Mode " of a SEv in the NvM .

The write routine of the NvM block NvM_WriteBlock shall be triggered after the modification of a " Reporting Mode " value IdsMReportingModeFilter has been successfully changed by the diagnostic services.
If the persistence in the NvM block fails, the IdsM shall roll back the SEv ’s "Reporting Mode" IdsMReportingModeFilter , to the value before the diagnostic modification.
The IdsM shall be able to read out the " Reporting Mode " IdsMReportingModeFilter persisted in the NvM for the corresponding SEvs handled by the IdsM instance.
In case there are no NvM values available for the " Reporting Mode " IdsMReportingModeFilter of the SEvs, the configured values provided in the configuration tool shall be used.
The NvM block descriptor referenced by IdsMNvmBlockDescriptor , shall be a block processed during NvM_ReadAll .
The supported NvM RAM block name shall be IdsM_NvMRamBlockData.
The supported NvM ROM block name shall be IdsM_NvMRomBlockData.
The diagnostic handling feature shall be optional. It shall be activated or deactivated with the parameter IdsMDiagnosticSupport .
Reporting Mode and Diagnostics The " Reporting Mode " IdsMReportingModeFilter of a SEv shall be modifiable during run-time via the diagnostic services of the Dcm .

Modify Reporting Mode via Diagnostics The service IdsM_Dcm_SetReportingMode_Start called by the Dcm module shall enable the IdsM to modify the Reporting Mode IdsMReportingModeFilter of a specific SEv . This service shall trigger the routine execution to modify the current " Reporting Mode ", and shall contain the new reporting mode value to be set.

Invalid Reporting Mode Parameter In case the reporting mode parameter in IdsM_Dcm_SetReportingMode_Start is invalid, this IdsM service shall return DCM_E_REQUESTOUTOFRANGE as its Dcm negative response and the function shall return E_NOT_OK .

Invalid Reporting Mode Parameter In case the Security Event Definition Id used for the call IdsM_Dcm_SetReportingMode_Start is invalid, this IdsM service shall return DCM_E_REQUESTOUTOFRANGE as its Dcm negative response and the function shall return E_NOT_OK .

Persist Failure In case the request to NvM to persist the new reporting mode fails, this IdsM service shall return DCM_E_GENERALPROGRAMMINGFAILURE as its Dcm negative response and the function shall return E_NOT_OK .
Roll Back in case of Failure In case the request to NvM to persist the new reporting mode fails, this IdsM service shall roll back to the previously configured reporting mode.
Readable Reporting Mode The "Reporting Mode" IdsMReportingModeFilter of a SEv shall be readable via the diagnostic services of the Dcm .
Reading Reporting Mode The service IdsM_Dcm_GetReportingMode_Start called by the Dcm module shall trigger the IdsM ’s routine execution to request the current reporting mode of a specific SEv .

Reporting Mode Result The service IdsM_Dcm_GetReportingMode_RequestResults called by the Dcm module shall allow the IdsM to provide the routine results and reporting mode for the requested security event via a result pointer.

Ifl library shall not require initialization phase. A Library function may be called at the very first step of ECU initialization, e.g. even by the OS or EcuM, thus the library shall be ready.
Ifl library shall not require a shutdown operation phase.
The Ifl library shall be implemented in a way that the code can be shared among callers in different memory partitions.
Usage of macros should be avoided. The function should be declared as function or inline function. Macro #define should not be used.
A library function can call other library functions because all library functions shall be re-entrant. A library function shall not call any BSW modules functions, e.g. the DET.
The library, written in C programming language, should conform to the MISRA C Standard. Please refer to SWS_BSW_00115 for more details.
Each AUTOSAR library Module implementation <library>*.c and <library>*.h shall map their code to memory sections using the AUTOSAR memory mapping mechanism.
Each AUTOSAR library Module implementation <library>*.c, that uses AUTOSAR integer data types and/or the standard return, shall include the header file Std_Types.h.
All AUTOSAR library Modules should use the AUTOSAR data types (integers, boolean) instead of native C data types, unless this library is clearly identified to be compliant only with a platform.
All AUTOSAR library Modules should avoid direct use of compiler and platform specific keyword, unless this library is clearly identified to be compliant only with a platform. eg. #pragma, typeof etc.
